items.title: Null-conditional assignment
items.text: Treat absence explicitly. Check null before dereferencing, use a deliberate fallback, and do not silence nullable warnings without evidence.

items.title: Expanded Span<T> and ReadOnlySpan<T> conversions
items.text: Check bounds and copy behavior. Index-from-end and ranges make positions concise but do not remove boundary requirements.

items.title: Unbound generic types with nameof
items.text: Generics preserve type information while letting one implementation work with many types. Constraints state requirements at compile time; variance changes assignment compatibility only in supported input/output positions.

items.title: Modifiers on simple lambda parameters
items.text: Pick a parameter-passing form that communicates ownership and intent; avoid ref/out when a returned value is clearer.

items.title: Partial events and constructors
items.text: Make required state explicit during object creation and keep partially initialized objects from escaping.

items.title: User-defined compound assignment operators
items.text: Know the operator rules, but add parentheses when they clarify the intended grouping for a reader.

items.title: File-based app support
items.text: Use explicit paths and scoped resource disposal; test missing files, permission failures, and partial data.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates c# 14 features. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates c# 14 features rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for c# 14 features before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
